content.text: {"grade": 6, "complete": false, "main_gap": "Xiang's explicit refinement construction (the overlay realizing D \u2264 \u0393 with at most q\u22121 cuts) is asserted as 'standard; details omitted'; the tight cut count is never verified.", "errors": [{"description": "Upper-bound half of the refinement lemma: the overlay/common-refinement construction is only sketched, with the crucial verification that it uses at most q\u22121 cuts (it needs |B| cuts in the A-row including one at s_B, |A|\u22121 in the B-row, plus q\u2212|A|\u2212|B| bisections) omitted entirely. This is the constructive core of Xiang's strategy.", "quote": "and use at most \\(q-1\\) cuts in total (standard; details omitted)."}, {"description": "The reduction 'deleting two equal entries from a sorted list does not change D' is stated rather than proved; it needs the observation that within a tie block the two copies can be taken adjacent and that repeated deletion keeps the list sorted. Correct but informal.", "quote": "Deleting two equal entries from a sorted list does not change \\(D\\): the two copies may be adjacent within their tie block"}], "notes": "Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) is consistent with an independent check at n=1,2. Drafting lemma and the graph/tree lower bound D \u2265 \u0393 are correct and carefully done. Sections 5\u20136 are non-mathematical padding but harmless."}
